title: Shepherd's Pie
subtitle: British minced lamb pie with mashed potato topping
excerpt: Shepherd's pie made the proper way: minced lamb braised with onion, carrot, and fresh rosemary until the filling is thick and deeply savoury, topped with fluffy mashed potato baked to a golden crust.

recipe.sourceNotes: Shepherd's pie is the lamb version of cottage pie; the shepherd name refers to the shepherd who tends the flock. The distinction is formal in British cooking: cottage pie is beef, shepherd's pie is lamb, and the two should not be confused. The dish likely developed as a way to use leftover roast lamb, minced and mixed with gravy. Modern recipes use raw mince from the outset, which produces a better, more consistent result. Rosemary is the essential flavouring for lamb; it is more assertive than the thyme used in cottage pie and stands up well to the gamey character of the meat. The dish makes excellent use of waxy or floury potatoes for the topping; floury varieties produce a lighter mash.

content.text: The distinction from cottage pie is the lamb and the rosemary; do not substitute other herbs. Use a higher-fat mince (around 20%) for a more flavourful filling. The filling should be cooked until quite thick before adding the potato topping; if it is too liquid, the topping will sink and the pie will be wet.

items.preparation: peeled and quartered; for the topping

content.text: Brown the mince in batches in the oil over high heat; do not crowd the pan. Remove each batch as it colours. Add the onion, carrot, celery, and garlic and cook for 8 minutes. Return the mince. Add tomato puree and flour. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add the stock, Worcestershire sauce, rosemary, and bay. Simmer uncovered for 25 to 30 minutes until the filling is thick and coats a spoon. Season. Preheat the oven to 200°C / fan 180°C / gas 6.
Boil the potatoes until tender. Drain, steam dry, and mash with butter and warm milk until smooth and fluffy. Season well.
Spoon the filling into a baking dish. Spread or pipe the mash over the top. Rough up the surface with a fork. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden on top and bubbling at the edges.
